witness.work: A Manual of Prayers for the Use of the Catholic Laity
witness.edition: New York, The Catholic Publication Society, 1888
witness.title: Prayer for Light Before Examination of Conscience
witness.full_text: O my God, sovereign Judge of men, who desirest not the death of a sinner, but that he should be converted and saved, enlighten my mind, that I may know the sins which I have this day committed in thought, word, or deed, and give me the grace of true contrition.
witness.preceding_rubric: Ask of God light to discover the sins committed this day.
witness.subsequent_rubric: Here examine your Conscience; then say:
witness.next_prayer_incipit: O my God, I heartily repent, and am grieved that I have offended Thee

identity_review.distinction: A prayer asking divine light is recited; a separate editorial examination guide is silent/reflection content; evening contrition follows. They must not be fused in one alleged 1888 prayer.
identity_review.note: Lasance prayer already petitions for light but simultaneously performs evening adoration and thanksgiving, so it is a different complete text, not a translation of Baltimore's short independent prayer.
